plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches still bare of leaves burst into fragrant blossoms. The flowers are delicate and five-petaled, and they open while winter's chill lingers. Their spicy-sweet perfume drifts through gardens and orchards, and they are among the first signs that spring is coming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, often peaking in mid-to-late February
plants.location: Japan, including the Kanto and Kansai regions, where ume groves and gardens are in bloom in late February
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms have been celebrated in East Asian poetry and art for more than a thousand years. In Japan, people also pickle the fruit into umeboshi and steep it in liqueur.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is one of the most dramatic flowers on Earth. A dinner-plate-sized crown of silky, pointed bracts surrounds a center of fine, feathery florets. It grows on rugged shrubs in the fynbos of South Africa's Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late winter through spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from roughly late summer into early summer depending on the variety and location
plants.funFact: King proteas evolved to survive wildfires. Their thick underground stems resprout after a burn, and the plant is South Africa's national flower.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding white bells with green-tipped inner petals push up through frost, and sometimes through snow. In woodlands and gardens across Europe they carpet the ground in drifts of white.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with a peak in February in much of Europe
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens in the United Kingdom and across Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make natural antifreeze-like proteins that help them cope with the cold. They also produce galantamine, a compound used in medicine for Alzheimer's disease.
